answer: Every hurdle the maker builds is entered against the coppice the hazel was cut from, with the rods counted and the date written. A plume hurdle bought from another county fails the record: at the tide of the rods the hazel must match the coppice the book names, and strange rods split wrong. Faking a hurdle means renting a coppice, cutting rods for a month and paying 5,300, and the ridge line in the coppice record is kept by the parish, so a hurdle whose rods were never counted is burned.
